items.title: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., United States: Foreign official holdings of U.S. Treasuries fell to 12.5% of total outstanding, the lowest this century, as marketable Treasury debt surged to $29.1 trillion and China's holdings dropped to $651.1 billion, the lowest since September 2008.
items.description: Foreign official holdings of U.S. Treasuries fell to 12.5% of total outstanding, the lowest this century, as marketable Treasury debt surged to $29.1 trillion and China's holdings dropped to $651.1 billion, the lowest since September 2008.
items.rawSummary: President Trump announced the removal of U.S. sanctions on Turkey and remained open to F-35 sales as domestic indicators highlighted rising joblessness fears, retreating foreign demand for Treasuries, and dwindling expectations for Fed rate cuts.
items.analysis: President Trump announced the United States is removing sanctions on Turkey, saying 'it's time' and that he does not want to sanction friends, a step that follows his consideration of F-35 sales and his characterization of Turkey as 'much more loyal' than other countries, undercutting Netanyahu's appeal to block the deal and matching a Reuters report that the administration would support the sale. Domestically, consumer sentiment pointed to rising unemployment fears, with the jobs plentiful-to-hard-to-find gap at its narrowest since 2020, and market odds of a Fed rate cut dropping to 21 percent. Trump announced Walmart would cut prices—including a near 15% drop on ground beef—for the US 250th anniversary and claimed broad declines in oil, gas, egg, and prescription drug costs. Fiscal pressures deepened as foreign official holdings of US Treasuries fell to their lowest share this century, while an OMFIF survey of central banks and sovereign funds managing over $10 trillion in assets showed that 4% plan to reduce US dollar exposure in the next 12-24 months, the first such reading in three years, and 82% of central banks now hold physical gold. Stress in private credit markets intensified with record redemption requests and plunging inflows, and Trump touted military recruiting records while calling on Congress to pass a $350 billion defense package and the 'Save America Act'. Unconfirmed reports indicated that Ayatollah Khamenei's funeral may take place in Najaf and Karbala, while the new Iraqi prime minister planned a Washington visit, adding potential volatility to the Iran-focused diplomatic agenda.

items.title: Qeshm Island and Strait of Hormuz coast, Iran, Iran: Another oil tanker was reportedly struck while transiting the Omani route despite U.S. Navy support, with tankers from Japan, India, and other nations consequently shifting to the Iran-controlled northern corridor.
items.description: Another oil tanker was reportedly struck while transiting the Omani route despite U.S. Navy support, with tankers from Japan, India, and other nations consequently shifting to the Iran-controlled northern corridor.
items.rawSummary: Iran’s IRGC struck at least four commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz over the past day, including a Qatari LNG tanker, prompting international condemnation, a shift of maritime traffic toward the Iran-controlled northern lane, and claims of a ceasefire violation, while the United States has yet to respond militarily.
items.analysis: In the early hours of July 7, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired missiles at two commercial vessels, striking a loaded Qatari LNG tanker and setting it ablaze, though no casualties were reported. Axios and U.S. officials confirmed the attack, and Iranian state television later said the ship had ignored warnings while using the southern U.S.-supported corridor, implying IRGC responsibility. Qatar’s foreign ministry condemned the targeting as an act of aggression against international navigation, adding a sharp diplomatic rebuke from a Gulf neighbor. U.S. officials signaled that retaliation is likely, but by late afternoon no military response had materialized, even as additional attacks unfolded: an oil tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile, another was struck by a one-way attack drone, and UK Maritime Trade Operations later confirmed two more vessels were struck, bringing the total to at least four commercial ships targeted in 24 hours. All later incidents caused minor damage and no casualties. The attacks were also characterized as a clear violation of existing ceasefire agreements. Meanwhile, vessels from Japan, India, and other nations began diverting to the Iran-controlled northern shipping lane, reinforcing Tehran's operational grip on strait traffic as Germany joined calls for freedom of navigation.

items.title: Turkey (NATO summit), Turkey: Rutte highlighted that Russia is spending almost half of its national budget on its war machine and warned of increasing cooperation between Russia, China, North Korea, and Iran.
items.description: Rutte highlighted that Russia is spending almost half of its national budget on its war machine and warned of increasing cooperation between Russia, China, North Korea, and Iran.
items.rawSummary: The NATO summit in Ankara saw major defense initiatives and a U.S. pledge to lift CAATSA sanctions on Turkey, alongside broader remarks on Greenland, European troop withdrawals, and Ukrainian calls for Patriot production licenses.
items.analysis: The summit opened with tens of billions in defence deals, a $40 billion Drone Edge Initiative, and artillery shell contracts to nearly double production, as Secretary General Rutte warned of Russia's military spending nearing half its budget and its deepening coordination with China, North Korea, and Iran, and as von der Leyen highlighted €150 billion in EU defence funds open to Turkish participation. Trump expressed disappointment with NATO, said he might not have attended without Erdoğan as host, announced he would lift CAATSA sanctions, calling it unwanted punishment of a friend, and Erdoğan welcomed the move while voicing confidence in receiving five F-35 jets after Trump gave his word. Trump dismissed concerns over Turkey's Russian S-400 systems and appeared unaware of any third-country relocation proposal, while also calling for U.S. control of Greenland and stating all American troops could leave Europe. Zelensky, citing deep drone strikes on Siberian refineries and massive Russian troop casualties, urged Europe to mass-produce anti-ballistic systems and called for U.S. Patriot production licenses. The sanctions removal and F-35 discussions signal a potential reset in U.S.-Turkey defence ties despite unresolved questions over the S-400.

items.title: Beijing, China: Reuters reports that China is considering restricting overseas access to advanced AI models, treating frontier AI as a strategic national asset, following meetings with companies including Alibaba and ByteDance.
items.description: Reuters reports that China is considering restricting overseas access to advanced AI models, treating frontier AI as a strategic national asset, following meetings with companies including Alibaba and ByteDance.
items.rawSummary: China conducted a submarine-launched ballistic missile test that drew U.S. criticism over its nuclear buildup, while Beijing considers restricting foreign access to advanced AI models.
items.analysis: The Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy announced a scheduled intercontinental-range ballistic missile test from a Type 09IV/A SSBN, the first such launch since 2024, with the unarmed missile landing in the Southern Pacific Ocean after Beijing pre-notified relevant nations. The United States monitored the test and the State Department issued a statement criticizing China's rapid and opaque nuclear expansion, urging meaningful arms control discussions and a regularized notification arrangement for all intercontinental-range ballistic missile and space launches consistent with other P5 members. The PLAN described the test as routine, though it comes amid broad strategic competition in the Indo-Pacific. Separately, Reuters reported that Beijing is considering restricting overseas access to its most advanced artificial intelligence models, treating frontier AI as a strategic national asset, following meetings with companies including Alibaba and ByteDance. These developments underscore China's heightened focus on controlling key military and technological capabilities.

items.description: BNO reported at least four fatalities, more than 170 injuries, and one person missing.
items.rawSummary: A tornado struck Huanggang, Hubei Province, causing fatalities, injuries, and widespread damage to homes and businesses.
items.analysis: A large tornado struck Huanggang in Hubei Province, China, on July 6, causing significant destruction to homes and businesses and injuring multiple people. BNO reported on July 7 that at least four people were killed, more than 170 were injured, and one person remains missing. Earlier accounts had indicated two fatalities and hundreds of injuries, and the full scale of damage and casualties is still being assessed. Emergency response efforts are continuing.

items.analysis: President Trump announced the United States is removing sanctions on Turkey, saying 'it's time' and that he does not want to sanction friends, a step that follows his consideration of F-35 sales and his characterization of Turkey as 'much more loyal' than other countries, undercutting Netanyahu's appeal to block the deal and matching a Reuters report that the administration would support the sale. Domestically, consumer sentiment pointed to rising unemployment fears, with the jobs plentiful-to-hard-to-find gap at its narrowest since 2020, and market odds of a Fed rate cut dropping to 21 percent. Trump announced Walmart would cut prices—including a near 15% drop on ground beef—for the US 250th anniversary and claimed broad declines in oil, gas, egg, and prescription drug costs. Fiscal pressures deepened as foreign official holdings of US Treasuries fell to their lowest share this century, while an OMFIF survey of central banks and sovereign funds managing over $10 trillion in assets showed that 4% plan to reduce US dollar exposure in the next 12-24 months, the first such reading in three years, and 82% of central banks now hold physical gold. Stress in private credit markets intensified with record redemption requests and plunging inflows, and Trump touted military recruiting records while calling on Congress to pass a $350 billion defense package and the 'Save America Act'. Unconfirmed reports indicated that Ayatollah Khamenei's funeral may take place in Najaf and Karbala, while the new Iraqi prime minister planned a Washington visit, adding potential volatility to the Iran-focused diplomatic agenda.
